views.name: yellow_trips_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id AS vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime AS pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime AS dropoff_datetime,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS trip_seconds,
  passenger_count AS passenger_count,
  SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS FLOAT64) AS trip_distance_miles,
  SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS FLOAT64) AS fare_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(extra AS FLOAT64) AS extra,
  SAFE_CAST(mta_tax AS FLOAT64) AS mta_tax,
  SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tip_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tolls_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tolls_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(imp_surcharge AS FLOAT64) AS imp_surcharge,
  SAFE_CAST(total_amount AS FLOAT64) AS total_amount,
  pickup_longitude AS pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude AS pickup_latitude,
  dropoff_longitude AS dropoff_longitude,
  dropoff_latitude AS dropoff_latitude,
  rate_code AS rate_code,
  store_and_fwd_flag AS store_and_fwd_flag,
  payment_type AS payment_type
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2016`
WHERE pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per yellow taxi trip record (as in source table)
views.description: Normalized projection of yellow taxi trips with cleaned timestamps, derived trip duration and fare components. Use when you need deterministic measures and preserved identifiers for joins or downstream aggregates. | Use for: aggregate trip durations or fares by time window; geospatial analyses of pickup/dropoff locations; filter trips by payment type or rate_code; compute tip rates or fare per mile

views.name: citibike_trips_normalized_station_ids
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tripduration AS trip_seconds,
  starttime AS starttime,
  stoptime AS stoptime,
  CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id_str,
  start_station_name AS start_station_name,
  CAST(end_station_id AS STRING) AS end_station_id_str,
  end_station_name AS end_station_name,
  start_station_latitude AS start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude AS start_station_longitude,
  end_station_latitude AS end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude AS end_station_longitude,
  bikeid AS bikeid,
  usertype AS usertype,
  birth_year AS birth_year,
  gender AS gender
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
WHERE starttime IS NOT NULL AND stoptime IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per citibike trip (as in source table)
views.description: Normalized citibike trips with station id stringified to match station dimension; compute trip duration seconds and preserve station coordinates. Use for joining trips to station metadata. | Use for: join trips to citibike_stations by station id; age/gender usage patterns; trip duration distributions by station

views.name: citibike_station_latest_status
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id AS station_id,
  ANY_VALUE(name) AS name,
  ANY_VALUE(short_name) AS short_name,
  ANY_VALUE(latitude) AS latitude,
  ANY_VALUE(longitude) AS longitude,
  ANY_VALUE(region_id) AS region_id,
  ANY_VALUE(rental_methods) AS rental_methods,
  ANY_VALUE(capacity) AS capacity,
  ANY_VALUE(eightd_has_key_dispenser) AS eightd_has_key_dispenser,
  ANY_VALUE(num_bikes_available) AS num_bikes_available,
  ANY_VALUE(num_bikes_disabled) AS num_bikes_disabled,
  ANY_VALUE(num_docks_available) AS num_docks_available,
  ANY_VALUE(num_docks_disabled) AS num_docks_disabled,
  MAX(last_reported) AS last_reported
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations`
GROUP BY station_id
grain: one row per station_id (latest snapshot aggregated)
views.description: Station-level latest status snapshot preserving capacity and availability measures. One row per station representing the most recently reported status (by last_reported). Use for current-state joins or capacity analyses. | Use for: current availability by station; capacity utilization across regions; joining station metadata to trips

views.name: nypd_collisions_by_day
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(timestamp) AS collision_date,
  borough AS borough,
  COUNT(1) AS collisions_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_persons_injured,0)) AS persons_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_persons_killed,0)) AS persons_killed,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_injured,0)) AS pedestrians_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_killed,0)) AS pedestrians_killed,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_injured,0)) AS cyclists_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_killed,0)) AS cyclists_killed,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_motorist_injured,0)) AS motorists_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed,0)) AS motorists_killed
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.nypd_mv_collisions`
GROUP BY collision_date, borough
views.description: Daily aggregated collision counts and injury/fatality sums by borough and date. Use when analyzing temporal trends in collisions and severity. | Use for: time series of collisions by borough; compare injury vs fatality trends; correlate collisions with other daily signals (311, trips)

views.name: svc311_geocoded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS unique_key,
  created_date AS created_date,
  closed_date AS closed_date,
  DATE(created_date) AS created_date_date,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM created_date) AS created_hour,
  agency AS agency,
  agency_name AS agency_name,
  complaint_type AS complaint_type,
  descriptor AS descriptor,
  status AS status,
  borough AS borough,
  incident_zip AS incident_zip,
  street_name AS street_name,
  incident_address AS incident_address,
  community_board AS community_board,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
grain: one row per 311 service request (as in source table)
views.description: 311 service requests with normalized date parts and safe latitude/longitude. Use for spatial joins or time-based analyses of 311 activity. | Use for: spatial clustering of complaint types; response time (created to closed) analyses; join with collisions or trips by location/time

views.name: yellow_trips_pickup_hour_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id AS vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime AS pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime AS dropoff_datetime,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS trip_seconds,
  passenger_count AS passenger_count,
  trip_distance AS trip_distance_miles,
  pickup_longitude AS pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude AS pickup_latitude,
  rate_code AS rate_code,
  store_and_fwd_flag AS store_and_fwd_flag,
  payment_type AS payment_type,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) AS pickup_hour,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) ORDER BY TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) ASC) AS hour_trip_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2016`
WHERE pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per yellow taxi trip with rank per pickup hour
views.description: Yellow trips augmented with pickup hour and a per-hour rank by trip_seconds (fastest trips get rank 1). Useful for Top-K or percentile filtering by hour. | Use for: top-k fastest/slowest trips per hour; filtering trips by rank within time buckets; hourly distribution of short trips

views.name: trees_with_species
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.recordid AS recordid,
  t.address AS address,
  t.house_number AS house_number,
  t.street AS street,
  t.borough AS borough,
  t.longitude AS longitude,
  t.latitude AS latitude,
  t.diameter AS diameter,
  t.status AS status,
  t.spc_common AS spc_common,
  t.spc_latin AS spc_latin,
  s.species_common_name AS species_common_name,
  s.species_scientific_name AS species_scientific_name,
  s.tree_size AS tree_size,
  s.growth_rate AS growth_rate
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995` AS t
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` AS s
  ON LOWER(TRIM(t.spc_common)) = LOWER(TRIM(s.species_common_name))
  OR LOWER(TRIM(t.spc_latin)) = LOWER(TRIM(s.species_scientific_name))
grain: one row per tree census record (as in source table)
views.description: Tree census records left-joined to species reference to expose common and scientific names and characteristics. One row per tree census record preserved. Use for ecological or spatial analyses of tree populations. | Use for: species distribution across boroughs; diameter distributions by species; matching census records to species characteristics
